3.text: will harmonize with each other; while the others perform quite individually,

4.text: without any attention to their fellows.

5.text: A man often summons a woman to dance with him, in which case he

6.text: spreads a skin on the ground for her to dance upon. After the performance,

7.text: this skin is taken by the woman. Other presents are also offered and ac-

8.text: cepted, especially when the man and the woman are cousins, or relatives of

10.text: When the performance is in full swing, the shamans begin to take part

11.text: in it, generally one by one, although at the end there may be two or three

12.text: acting at the same time. Their acting, of course, consists of magical arts.

13.text: They beat the drum with violence and persistence, and their songs are

14.text: strangely complicated, because the tunes of shamans generally admit of con-

15.text: siderable variations. Their motions, too, are violent and irregular, befitting

16.text: those who feel the approach of “spirits.”

17.text: At last the “spirits” come and enter the bodies of their servants. From

18.text: that time on, the shamans are supposed to assume the appearance of the

19.text: supernatural beings that have entered them. They act accordingly, shake

20.text: their heads violently, and produce the gibbering noise mentioned before, which

21.text: is supposed to be the voice of the “spirits.”¹ In case some particular “spirit”
21.note: Footnote reference marker ¹ (U+00B9) keyed tight against the closing quote, per §2.10; anchors the note on line 43.

22.text: of theirs is a bear, a raven, or a wolf, they try to imitate also its motions and

23.text: cries. I have heard several times that powerful shamans even wrap the body

24.text: in a bear-skin taken off whole for this purpose, or put a raven’s beak on the

25.text: face. Then they turn temporarily into bears or ravens, and act like such.

26.text: This may be considered in connection with what was said about the ceremo-

27.text: nial concerning the wolf or bear killed and brought home. Nevertheless, I

28.text: had no opportunity to witness such performances: therefore I am not able to

29.text: say how far the information collected corresponds to the rites actually

31.text: I am not aware that any disguise in the form of special garments or

32.text: masks is used. Those shamans, indeed, who have a special dress, use it on

33.text: such occasions; and sometimes an ordinary person may have a special garment,

34.text: made by the advice of a shaman, as a protection against disease or misfor-

35.text: tune. This will be supplied with tassels and pendants in the nature of charms.

36.text: I heard of shamans performing the ceremonial in their own family quite naked;

37.text: but this is undoubtedly connected with some details of Chukchee shamanism

38.text: of which I shall speak later.
